cues: Sound collected by the pinna vibrates the ear drum.
Three tiny bones, the malleus, incus and stapes, the smallest in the body, act as levers and amplify the vibration about twenty times.
The stapes pushes on the oval window, sending waves through the fluid of the cochlea, where hair cells in the organ of Corti turn them into nerve impulses.
We hear from twenty to twenty thousand hertz.
